title: Singulate the middle box from a tightly packed 3 x 3 cluster and put it on the pad
instruction: Put the blue box from the middle of the cluster on the green pad. Keep the other eight boxes on the grey mat the whole time, each sitting flat on the mat, not on another box.
context: Order pickers and piece-picking robots with finger grippers often face items packed side to side (a suction cup could lift one from above; fingers cannot). The middle item cannot be gripped until room is made beside it by moving its neighbours, and they must stay flat on the mat while that is done.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases (which are 61 cm apart). Grey mat (fixed, grey rubber sheet taped to the table): 310 mm front to back and 320 mm wide, 2 mm thick, spanning 12.0 to 43.0 cm in front of the arm bases and from 4.0 cm right of the midline to 28.0 cm left of it. Cubes (loose): nine cardboard boxes, each a 50 mm cube of 60 g, sitting on the mat in a 3 x 3 square with their sides square to the table, packed side to side (0.2 mm between neighbours, so no finger fits between them). The square's centre cube is blue and stands 32.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 17.0 cm left of the midline; the other eight are brown and stand at 50.2 mm pitch around it, so the square spans 24.5 to 39.5 cm in front and 9.5 to 24.5 cm left of the midline. Green pad (fixed, green card taped to the table): 80 x 80 mm, 2 mm thick, centred 20.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 34.5 cm left of the midline (20 cm in front of the left arm's base and 4 cm to its left), 25 mm beyond the mat's left edge. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: All limits are inclusive. At rest: moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s. Flat: highest point at most 53 mm above the lowest (about 3.4 degrees). A brown cube is on the mat when it is flat, its bottom is within 3 mm of the mat's top and its centre is over the mat. The brown cubes are intact when all eight are on the mat at every step of the trial and at rest at the end: one lifted more than 3 mm, stacked, tipped past flat or with its centre pushed past the mat's edge even for a moment fails the trial, even if put back in its place. Only an episode reset clears this record (every cube within 0.5 mm of its start and at rest, reached by a jump of over 50 mm in one control step). With the brown cubes intact: 1.0 if the blue cube lies flat wholly inside the green pad's edges, its bottom within 1 mm of the pad's top, at rest; 0.5 if its centre is off the mat and it lies flat and at rest with its bottom within 1 mm of the table, or with its centre over the pad and its bottom within 1 mm of the pad's top. 0.25 if it lies flat on the mat at rest (bottom within 1 mm of the mat's top, centre over the mat) with a 15 mm strip clear of other cubes along each of two opposite side faces (touching the strip's outer edge is allowed). Otherwise 0, including the blue cube on the mat without that room, held, moving, tilted or on another cube. The trial ends at 1.0 once that has held for 1 s; otherwise the last step is scored.
reset_notes: 1. Leave the grey mat and the green pad taped in place; nothing is consumed. 2. Take all nine cubes off the mat and the pad. 3. Set the blue cube flat on the mat with its centre 32.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 17.0 cm left of the midline, sides square to the table. 4. Set the eight brown cubes flat around it at 50.2 mm pitch, packed side to side with about 0.2 mm between neighbours, so the square spans 24.5 to 39.5 cm in front and 9.5 to 24.5 cm left of the midline. 5. Check that no cube sits on another and nothing else is on the table. In simulation, runs use object_jitter=0, which this task needs: jitter would break the packed square.
fidelity: Approximate. Boxes are rigid cubes with the simulator's friction, not cardboard that crushes or bends; real cartons vary in size, so real packed clusters have uneven gaps. The mat and pad are fixed thin boxes. The 0.2 mm gaps stand in for touching boxes. Mass and friction are not measured from real boxes.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (re-scored under the revised scorer: it scored 0.0 under the same tiers, and the new rule only adds a way to fail); demo: 1.0 (rerun under the revised scorer, every brown cube flat on the mat at every step)
